newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Novartis seeks China partners.
newsitem.headline: Novartis seeks China partners.

text.p: Novartis, the Swiss pharmaceutical company to arise from the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG, said on Thursday it is actively searching for partnerships in China.
But Novartis president designate Daniel Vasella said the respect of intellectual property rights was a fundamental condition for developing closer links.
"We would like to establish more and closer links," Vasella told reporters in Hong Kong.
He said Novartis' current investment in China totals more than US$100 million. "But I would say what is more important is what we will invest in the future," he said.

"I think we will see a shift...from a focus on purely manufacturing...to more production of value through intellectual work," Vasella said. But he said the company "cannot have doubts about intellectual property".
"I believe there is a commitment from the government to respect the law. But the country is huge and it is partly decentralised," he said.
The group is currently collaborating with the Academy of Military Medicine Science in Beijing on an anti-malaria compound. Registration of the product is expected during the second half of 1997.
Among other ventures, Novartis has two crop protection joint ventures in China and an animal health joint venture in Shanghai.

The group's sales in the Asia/Australia/Africa account for 21 percent of the global sales. Novartis said it has proforma market share of 2.9 percent in South East Asia compared to global market share of 4.4 percent.
